query: What pre-specified subgroup contrasts, minimum subgroup sample sizes, and adaptive supports should be defined to detect and remediate inequitable effects across student groups?

response.query: What pre-specified subgroup contrasts, minimum subgroup sample sizes, and adaptive supports should be defined to detect and remediate inequitable effects across student groups?
response.answer: Define pre-specified subgroup contrasts by race, gender, and socioeconomic status; set minimum subgroup sample sizes of 100; use adaptive remediative strategies to address inequities.

results.title: Non-Compete Clause Rule
results.content: Specifically, the final rule provides that, with respect to a worker other than a senior executive, it is an unfair method of competition for a person to enter into or attempt to enter into a non-compete clause; to enforce or attempt to enforce a non-compete clause; or to represent that the worker is subject to a non-compete clause.[8]  The Commission describes the basis for its finding that these practices are unfair methods of competition in Parts IV.B.1 through IV.B.3. Estimated as 80% \* 18.1% \* 66% \* (33,271,644-27,151,987), where 80% is the percentage of covered workers (see Part X.F.4.a), 18.1% is the estimated percentage of workers with non-competes (see Starr, Prescott, & Bishara, *supra* note 68), 67% is the assumed percent of workers without digital contact information, and 6,119,657 = 33,271,644-27,151,987 is the count of workers at small businesses (see *https://advocacy.sba.gov/​wp-content/​uploads/​2023/​11/​2023-Small-Business-Economic-Profile-US.pdf*).
